Front: Subsets template: {{c1::def backtrack(start, path): result.append(path.copy()); for i in range(start, len(nums)): path.append(nums[i]); backtrack(i + 1, path); path.pop()}}
Subsets II (with dups) - skip: {{c1::if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue}}
Permutations with used array: {{c1::for i in range(len(nums)): if used[i]: continue; used[i] = True; path.append(nums[i]); backtrack(path); path.pop(); used[i] = False}}

Permutations with swap: {{c1::def backtrack(start): if start == len(nums): result.append(nums.copy()); for i in range(start, len(nums)): nums[start], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[start]; backtrack(start + 1); nums[start], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[start]}}
Permutations II (with dups) - skip: {{c1::if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1]: continue}}
Combinations template: {{c1::def backtrack(start, path): if len(path) == k: result.append(path.copy()); return; for i in range(start, n + 1): path.append(i); backtrack(i + 1, path); path.pop()}}
Combination Sum (reuse allowed): {{c1::for i in range(start, len(candidates)): if candidates[i] > remain: break; path.append(candidates[i]); backtrack(i, path, remain - candidates[i]); path.pop()}}
Combination Sum II (no reuse): {{c1::backtrack(i + 1, ...)}} instead of backtrack(i, ...)
Letter combinations of phone: {{c1::def backtrack(i, path): if i == len(digits): result.append(path); return; for c in mapping[digits[i]]: backtrack(i + 1, path + c)}}

Front: Time complexity of Subsets?
Back: O(n * 2^n) - 2^n subsets, O(n) to copy each

Front: Time complexity of Permutations?
Back: O(n * n!) - n! permutations, O(n) to copy each

Front: Time complexity of N-Queens?
Back: O(n!) with pruning

Front: Time complexity of Word Search?
Back: O(m * n * 4^L) where L is word length

Front: Space complexity of backtracking?
Back: O(n) for recursion depth + O(result size)

Front: Why copy path before adding to result?
Back: Path is modified during backtracking; without copy, all results would be same reference

Front: Why sort before handling duplicates?
Back: Brings duplicates together so we can skip consecutive same values

Front: What's the difference between subsets and combinations?
Back: Subsets: all sizes. Combinations: specific size k

Front: Why use 'not used[i-1]' for permutation duplicates?
Back: Ensures we only use duplicate after previous duplicate was used (ordering)
